answer.exemplar: Naming says the sentence repeats a phrase four times. Diagnosing says those four repetitions put the committee at the head of every clause, so a reader cannot tell which finding is which, and that is a different object to work on: cut the phrase, or restructure the sentence so the findings are distinguished. The second tells the writer which of those two moves to make and how to check whether it worked.

questions.explanation: Naming a weakness in a draft is a location, and diagnosing its cause is the mechanism behind it; only the second tells the writer what to do and how to know whether the fix worked, because four repetitions can be cured by four different operations and choosing wrongly wastes the revision. The tempting reading assumes a precisely worded complaint is already a diagnosis, since careful phrasing feels like analysis; phrasing tells the reader where to look and diagnosis tells the reader what the looking revealed, and a writer who has only the first has been sent to a place rather than given a task.
questions.hint: Ask which of the two hands the writer a choice between operations.
questions.learningObjective: explain the difference between naming a weakness and diagnosing its cause

questions.explanation: The diagnosis names the mechanism: the committee is the subject of every clause, so the three findings lose their separate subjects and a reader cannot tell which result is which. Cut the phrase and the sentence still has three findings with no subjects, which is why the other three replies leave the problem in place. The tempting reading prefers the prescription, on the theory that telling a writer what to do is more useful than explaining; a prescription chosen without a cause is a guess about a symptom, and a guess has to be tested by the writer rather than by the reviewer.

questions.explanation: The tone of that note makes being told the truth expensive: the writer now has to weigh a correct criticism against the risk of another one, and a reasonable response is to leave the draft alone and not attempt the revision. The bluntness buys nothing, because a note that names a sentence can be just as direct without passing a verdict on the writer. The tempting reading approves of the honesty, and there is a real fault in the draft; but honesty is a matter of naming the fault accurately, and the note spends its force on the writer instead of on the passage, which is the one place where force would have been useful.

questions.explanation: The description is what makes the judgment checkable: once a note has said what the text does, a writer can go and look and decide whether the verdict is fair, and a writer who disagrees can say precisely where. A judgment offered on its own has to be taken on trust, which is the definition of an instruction to guess. The tempting reading puts the order down to politeness, since description sounds like the milder half; the sequence is not a matter of temperature at all, it is the order in which a note becomes checkable, and reversing it produces a note that can only be obeyed or ignored.

questions.explanation: This chain is what makes a piece of feedback diagnostic rather than merely corrective, and it runs from address to effect to mechanism to operation to intent, with each step supplying the input the next one needs: an operation attached to no cause is a guess, and a cause named with no effect attached is an observation. The final question exists because the same shift may be deliberate, and only the writer knows. The tempting reading starts with the cause, since the diagnosis is the interesting part; but a cause reported without an address cannot be found, and a cause reported without an effect gives the writer no way to tell whether they understood what went wrong.

questions.explanation: An approval says the claim is good; a conditional says the claim is good provided a particular move stays where it is, which tells the writer both that the move is load-bearing and what will happen if it is moved. That is a finding about the draft, and the writer can check it by trying the reversal. The tempting reading hears a hedge, as though the peer had softened an objection into a qualified approval; nothing here is being softened, because the peer is not approving the claim but specifying the conditions of the claim, which is more information than a bare yes.
